summary: Pole tower with an L-4 cab, built 1937 on the Kaniksu National Forest; abandoned after 1950 and destroyed in 1962, with debris reported on site.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1962. A visitor's photo on Idaho Fire Lookouts shows debris at the site.

events.note: 50-ft pole tower with L-4 cab, per Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com. Forest Lookouts' 1962 item says the CCC built the group of towers in the 1930s.
Bobby Reed, per a Bonners Ferry Herald item quoted by Idaho Fire Lookouts and listed by firelookout.com.
Not used or maintained since 1950, per the 1962 news item quoted by Forest Lookouts.
A June 1962 Sandpoint News Bulletin item says the towers were being toppled and burned.

evidence.supports: White Mountain among six lookouts being toppled and destroyed
evidence.quote: The abandoned U.S. forest service lookouts on Strawberry mountain, White mountain, Katka peak, Buck mountain, Bald Eagle mountain and McCormick ridge are in the process of being toppled and destroyed.

evidence.supports: built by the CCC in the 1930s
evidence.quote: They were built in the 1930s by the Civilian Conservation Corps
have not been used or maintained since 1950 when the forest service went to aerial patrol
The towers are now being toppled and burned by district fire control officer Eugene H. Napier

evidence.supports: reader photo shows debris from burning
evidence.quote: quite a bit of debris present after being burned

evidence.supports: reader photo shows battery parts, post bases and concrete stairs
evidence.quote: most notably many electrical battery components and the post bases as well as a short set of condrete stairs

evidence.supports: reader reports abandoned helipad beside site
evidence.quote: There is an abandoned helipad adjacent to the tower site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says the 1930s, and Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com say 1937. The 1937 date is the more specific one and does not conflict.

notes_for_editor: Dates and destruction are consistent across three pages. The 1942 staff name and the 1962 burning are single-source. The debris description is an undated visitor comment on Idaho Fire Lookouts, not a survey; the story says so. Record elevation_m is null; the pages give 5,005 ft (about 1,525 m). One web search found no other source for this lookout. The Forest Lookouts item quotes a 1962 Sandpoint News Bulletin article, which was not read directly. The reader comment is spelled 'condrete' in the source; the story writes 'concrete'.
